name: Appam
subtitle: Lacy fermented rice pancakes with a soft, thick centre

ingredients.note: helps the batter ferment and spread

prepNotes: Appam batter ferments like dosa batter but is thinner and sweeter. It should pour, not spread.
The pan matters: a deep, round-bottomed appachatti is what makes the edges lacy and the centre thick. A small wok is the closest substitute.

steps.text: Grind the soaked rice with the grated coconut, cooked rice and enough water to make a smooth, pourable batter.
Add sugar, cover, and leave to ferment 8-10 hours until risen and faintly sour.
Stir in the coconut milk and salt. The batter should be thinner than dosa batter — like single cream.
steps.tip: Too thick and you get a pancake; too thin and it will not hold a centre.

steps.text: Heat the appachatti, wipe with coconut oil, pour a ladle into the middle, then immediately lift the pan and swirl it once so batter climbs the sides.
Cover and cook 2-3 minutes on low. Do not flip.
steps.tip: The lid is what steams the thick centre while the edges crisp.

steps.text: Lift out when the edges lift away on their own. Serve with stew, kadala curry or sweetened coconut milk.

storage: Batter keeps 3 days refrigerated and grows more sour; older batter suits appam less well than dosa. Cooked appams do not keep.
